ayahOccurrences.text: قَالَ هِىَ عَصَاىَ أَتَوَكَّؤُا۟ عَلَيْهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَىٰ غَنَمِى وَلِىَ فِيهَا مَـَٔارِبُ أُخْرَى
ayahOccurrences.highlightedHtml: قَالَ هِىَ عَصَاىَ أَتَوَكَّؤُا۟ عَلَيْهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَىٰ غَنَمِى وَلِىَ فِيهَا مَـَٔارِبُ أُخْرَى

lexSnapshot.derivativeNote: وَأَهُشُّ is in the derivative form: أَهُشُّ
lexSnapshot.rootDefinitionHtml:
هـ/ش/ش   h–sh–sh to be brittle; to be pliant, (of bread etc.) to be thin, to be soft; to be welcoming, to wear a welcoming smile; to drive away; to beat down tree leaves with a stick; a horse that perspires too much. Of this root, أَهُشُّ ʾahushshu occurs 1 time in the Qur’an
.
lexSnapshot.mainDefinitionHtml:
أَهُشُّ ʾahushshu [imperf. of v. هَشَّ hashsha] to beat down tree leaves; to drive away, to restrain

(20:18) قَالَ هِيَ عَصَايَ أَتَوَكَّأُ عَلَيْهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَى غَنَمِي he said, ‘It is my staff; I lean on it and I beat down leaves with it for my sheep (or, I restrain my sheep with it).’
